title: fix(app-shell): package-less app chrome readers read the names-only object scope (objectui#12980 part 6)
body:
Part of #12980
Clause-②: no

Part 6 of the card: part 1's leftover 1, the chrome hooks that still read the whole object registry (`GET /api/v1/meta/object`) in an app whose served item names no package. Two of the three hooks now read the names-only object scope there. The third, `useNavMemberGates`, is left as it is and reported as a fork (below).

## Measured first

- **P0, are package-less apps real?** Yes. The console's own Create App page (`CreateAppPage` in `@object-ui/plugin-designer`) saves with `client.meta.saveItem('app', draft.name, appSchema)` and names no package. objectstack serves a stored row bound to no package without `_packageId`: `withRowBinding` / `boundPackageOf` in `metadata-protocol` add no binding for such a row, and `DERIVED_PROVENANCE_KEYS` strips any stored copy. `AppManagementPage` already handles "a package-less app" for its writes. The showcase and CRM example apps are package-stamped (`stampPackage` in `engine.ts`), so they are not package-less.
- **P1, what does each hook need in such an app?** Context first: on an object route, a package-less app's `AppContent` reads the whole registry anyway (`readAppObjectScope` returns no scope without a package). The page route is the one route where such an app reads the names-only scope (`readPageObjectScope`). There, each hook's whole-registry read is the only one. Measured in a rendered test before the fix: one bare `object` call per mount from `useServedViewItems` / `useObjectPresence`, and one from `useNavMemberGates`.
  - `useObjectPresence(name)`: class (a). It needs exactly one name, the one it is asked about.
  - `useServedViewItems()`: class (a). It needs object documents only for the open view's object, on view routes, where the whole registry is read anyway. On a page route it needs none. It reads the names-only scope through the app's `requiresObject` names, which `AppContent` asks on every scoped route, so it adds no request. An app that requires no object reads nothing, the same way `readPageObjectScope` reads nothing for a page that binds no object.
  - `useNavMemberGates()`: **fork, not changed.** See open question.

## What changed

- `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useObjectPresence.ts`: when the app has a name and no `_packageId`, and the `object` type is still idle, presence is asked through `readObjectScope({ names: [name] })`.
- `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useServedViewItems.ts`: on the same condition, the served object documents are `readObjectScope({ names: requiresObjectNames }).served`, or none when the app requires no object.
- Outside an app (an empty `app`, as on the home page), and once anything has loaded the whole registry, both read the whole registry as before. Inside a package app nothing changes. `readObjectScope` is unchanged, and nothing new is exported.
- `.changeset/12980-packageless-chrome-scope.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`.

## Open question: `useNavMemberGates` is a fork

The order's stop rule applies: the derived name set and the whole registry answer the capability gate differently for some nav items.

- The gate is shared. `activityObjectRoster` (the bell's activity feed) runs it over **every** app's navigation and areas. With the whole registry, another app's entry whose `requiresObject` the runtime lacks is hidden. Measured: `checkCapability('object', 'other_missing')` answered `false`. With a names-only scope of this app's `requiresObject` names, that name is neither served nor missing, so it reads as registered (`registeredObjectNames.has(name) || !missingObjectNames.has(name)`).
- The app's own `areas[].navigation` entries are not named either. `readAppObjectScope` names `requiresObject` from `app.navigation` only, while `UnifiedSidebar` draws areas too.
- Options (the four-axis analysis is in the report on the card):
  - A: leave the hook as it is.
  - B: use this app's `requiresObject` names and accept the roster divergence, as package apps already do.
  - C: use the union of `requiresObject` across every app's navigation and areas. This is a closed set read from the app list, exact for every gate, at one by-name read per distinct required object.
- Until this is ruled, a package-less app's page open still reads the whole registry once, from the sidebar's gate. The two changed hooks then share that read and add no request.

## Tests

`packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/packagelessChromeScope-12980.test.tsx`, 6 tests:
- (a) In a package-less app, presence is read by name (present and absent), the served documents come from the names-only scope, and there is no bare `object` call.
- (a) An app that requires no object reads no served document and asks nothing.
- CONTROL: a package app gives `object?package=app.crm` + `object/sys_activity`, as in #12811.
- CONTROL: outside an app, the only call is `object`.
- CONTROL: once the whole registry is loaded, both hooks read it.

**Ablation**, once per changed hook, through `ablation-replace.mjs` with a trap restore:
- `useObjectPresence`: the condition narrowed back to `packageId`. All three (a) tests went red (`expected [ 'object/note', 'object' ] to not include 'object'`). The three CONTROLs stayed green. Restored blob `55f29b78ee2a` equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- `useServedViewItems`: the package-less branch disabled. All three (a) tests went red (`expected [ 'object' ] to not include 'object'`). The CONTROLs stayed green. Restored blob `964149b01cd7` equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Gates, at head `38c40e92bc`

- Targeted vitest, 11 files and 75 tests passed, exit 0. The files: the new test, plus every test file naming `useNavMemberGates` / `useServedViewItems` / `useObjectPresence` / `objectPresence` / `pageRouteObjects-12980`, plus `MetadataProvider.namesOnlyScope-12980`. That includes `AppContent.pageRouteObjects-12980`, `AppContent.objectScope-12811`, `scopedRegistryReaders-12811` and `openPathObjectReaders-12811`.
- Closure build `--filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...'`: exit 0. `@object-ui/app-shell` `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `--listFiles` shows the new test and both hooks in the test project.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the 3 changed files: 3 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The repo's eslint config is not type-aware, so this diff cannot change the verdict for any untouched file.
- Pre-tsc battery: every listed `check:*` passed with exit 0, as did `check-hand-rolled-comment-mask`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-presence` and `check:new-line-citations`.
- Declared to CI: the full `packages/app-shell/` directory and the repo-wide lint. The order rules out whole-package runs locally.

## Acceptance notes

- `useObjectPresence`'s scope path, now shared by package and package-less apps, reads a failed by-name fetch as `absent`. `getItem` turns any error into `null`, and `fetchScopeName` records `null` as missing. The module's own contract says an error is `unknown`. The whole-registry path keeps that contract: `error` reads `unknown`. This is pre-existing on the package path. The fix lives in `MetadataProvider`, outside this surface.
- `RecordFormPage` mounts its own `ExpressionProvider` with `app={{ name }}` and no `_packageId`. Its subtree (`ObjectForm`) renders neither changed hook, so it is unaffected.
